01 System map

Bangla name: সিস্টেম ম্যাপ

← Contents

The one page that shows how a customer, a member of staff or a background worker moves through GoBCB. Every feature file in this documentation drills into one box on this map. Read this first if you are new to the platform; if you already know it, use it as the index for finding the right feature file.

1. The three clients

Client Technology Who uses it Lives in Feature files
Admin portal Angular (standalone components, signals) GoBCB staff — event managers, admins rvl-gobcb-admin-portal/ 10 · Admin portal (A-01…A-31)
User portal Angular, SSR-capable Customers buying on the web rvl-gobcb-user-portal/ 20 · User portal (P-01…P-13)
User app Flutter, 3 packages Customers on Android / iOS rvl-gobcb-user-app/ 30 · User app (U-01…U-10)
Checker app Flutter, monorepo + vendored scanner Gate staff rvl-gobcb-checker-app/ 40 · Checker app (C-01…C-06)

The backend is a fifth repository, rvl-gobcb-backend/, holding nine ASP.NET Core 8 services plus two stubs. It is not a "client" but it is where every feature's real behaviour lives.

The five repositories in the workspace are rvl-gobcb-backend, rvl-gobcb-admin-portal, rvl-gobcb-user-portal, rvl-gobcb-user-app and rvl-gobcb-checker-app. They are git submodules and are treated as read-only by this documentation.

2. The backend services

Service Prefix Port Owns Feature files
Admin /admin 5101 All master data — programs, venues, events, pricing, layouts, promo codes, discounts, staff users, gate assignment, content, activity log A-01 … A-31
Booking /booking 5102 Capacity, seats, booking orders, DgePay payment, promo application, reservations, VAT challan P-04, P-06, S-05
Event /event 5103 The public read-only view the portals and app read P-01, U-02
Ticketing /ticketing 5108 Ticket generation, TSP signing, PDFs, downloads, OneID sync, offline-sold tickets P-09, S-08
TicketChecker /ticketChecker 5107 The checker's scan sync C-02, C-05
UserIssue /userissue 5110 Customer issues and the support chat hub P-12, U-08
PushNotification /pushnotification 5105 Device tokens and push send U-09, X-23
Scheduler /scheduler 5106 Workers only — no controllers S-11 … S-15
Utility /utility 5111 Worker only — merges and zips reserved tickets S-09
Platform /platform 5104 Stub — only a template WeatherForecastController —
UserAuth /userAuth 5109 Stub — only /health —

Every service is reached through its path prefix, added by GlobalRoutePrefixConvention (Application:ServiceName in appsettings.json) and terminated at the nginx ingress. So a controller route tickets/sync-tickets in TicketChecker is externally /ticketchecker/api/v1/tickets/sync-tickets.

Each service has its own DbContext and connection string, but all of them use the PostgreSQL schema etp. Tables that one service only reads are mapped with ExcludeFromMigrations so it does not try to own their schema — see X-19 and Q-02.

3. The three actors

Actor Cognito pool Reaches Token Feature files
Staff Admin pool (admin) /admin, and /ticketchecker for gate work admin JWT, policy- and role-scoped X-01, X-14, X-15, X-16
Customer User pool (user) /event, /booking, /ticketing, /userissue, /pushnotification, plus the external identity API and OneID user JWT X-06, X-07, X-10
Checker Ticket-checker pool (ticket-checker) /admin/ticket-checker-gate/event-info, /ticketchecker checker JWT X-12, C-01
Agent Agent pool (agent) POST /ticketing/api/v1/offline-sold-ticket agent JWT X-13 — no client exists in the workspace (Q-07)

Clients send the token in Authorization: Bearer; the Angular interceptor adds a static API-key header on an allow-list of routes, and the Flutter clients add their own per service (X-19).

5. The messaging backbone

Six SQS queues carry the asynchronous work. Each has a producer and a consumer, and the pairing is where most of the "why did this not happen yet" answers live.

Queue Produced by Consumed by Feature
OrderSuccess Booking, on a confirmed payment Ticketing TicketGenerationService S-07
EventCapacity Booking, on a seat lock change Booking LevelCapacityUpdateService, EventLiveCapacityUpdateService S-01, S-02
VatChallanProcessing Booking, on a Paid callback Scheduler VatChallanProcessingService S-10
TicketSigning Ticketing, when a PDF needs signing Ticketing S-08
TicketProcessing Ticketing, for reserved-ticket merges Utility TicketProcessingService S-09
FirebaseNotification PushNotification Scheduler FirebaseNotificationService S-11

All six are documented in 50 · System-initiated (S-01…S-17). Two behaviours are common to all of them and worth knowing before you debug one: there is no dead-letter handling in code, and the retry counter is incremented on a deserialised copy and never re-published, so a permanently failing message retries for ever (Q-09).

6. The request journeys

The four journeys below are the ones a new engineer should be able to narrate. Each is expanded in the linked file.

6.1 A customer buys a ticket — the longest path

User portal / App
  → Event service      browse programs, events, prices        P-01, P-02
  → Booking service    lock seats in Redis, create order     P-04, P-06
  → DgePay             redirect, pay, callback               P-06
  → (OrderSuccess queue)
  → Ticketing          generate PDFs, sign with TSP, ZIP     S-07, S-08, S-09
  → (FirebaseNotification queue) → Scheduler → FCM          S-11, S-12
  → Customer           download or view the signed PDF       P-09, U-06

Capacity is Redis-first (level_live, level_locked, 12-minute lock) with the database as the durable copy reconciled by workers — X-25, S-03.

6.2 A checker validates a ticket at the gate — the offline path

Checker app
  → Admin service     GET ticket-checker-gate/event-info     C-01
  → TicketChecker     POST sync-tickets  (download)         C-02
  → (local SQLite)    every scan is decided offline         C-03
  → TicketChecker     POST sync-tickets  (every 90 s)       C-05

This is the only journey that needs no network to be correct — that is the design intent, and it is why C-06 and C-04 matter so much: they are the paths where a decision is made with weaker evidence.

6.3 Staff set up an event

Admin portal
  → Admin service      programs, venues, layouts, pricing    A-01…A-14
  → Admin service      events, capacity, publishing          A-07…A-10
  → Event service      the published result becomes public   P-01, U-02

There is an ordering constraint that is enforced only in the UI: layouts must be published before an event can be published (Q-23, A-13).

6.4 A customer reports an issue

User portal / App
  → UserIssue service  POST /user-issue (the issue)         P-12, U-08
  → SignalR hub        /userissue/chathub  (authorised)     P-12, U-08
  → UserIssue service  REST fallback (NOT authorised)       Q-46
  → Admin portal       A-24 reads and resolves the issue     A-24

7. The cross-cutting concerns

Twenty-six concerns apply to more than one feature. They are in 60 · Cross-cutting.

Area Files Read it when
Authentication X-01 … X-04, X-06 … X-10, X-12 You need to know who the caller is, or how a login works
Authorization X-14 … X-17, X-18 You are deciding whether a screen should be reachable. Read X-18 before assuming an endpoint is protected.
Infrastructure X-19, X-20, X-25, X-26 You are changing a connection string, a file path, a Redis key or a config key
Messaging and notifications X-22, X-23, X-24 You are adding a notification or an audit trail
Feature-specific auth X-05, X-08, X-09, X-11, X-13 The specific flow, not the general rule

8. Where the risk is

If you read only one section of this handover, read this one. These are the places where the code is doing something that a reasonable person would not expect, ranked by consequence.

Risk Where Query
An unauthenticated endpoint lets anyone post support messages as an admin UserIssue chat REST controller Q-46
PushNotification has no authentication at all service-wide Q-04, Q-62
Admin-authored HTML is stored and rendered unsanitised content editor, notices, and two app widgets Q-33, Q-55
Manual ticket entry skips signature verification and writes a row even for unknown ids checker app Q-75
Duplicate tickets can be admitted at the same gate — detection is local only checker app Q-74
A paid-but-late order can be cancelled with money taken Booking re-check worker Q-11
A late payment callback records VAT for an order that stays unpaid Booking callback Q-15
The -1 manual-entry convention is undocumented on the server checker sync Q-68
iOS cannot verify any QR — the checker app is Android-only for real validation AppDelegate.swift Q-72
Database content is never translated — only the portal chrome switches language user portal Q-44
A failed sync still shows a "last sync time" checker app Q-76
The identity API — a large part of customer-facing behaviour — has no source in the workspace external Q-01
